items.title: FAA Grants Commercial Operating Certificate to McKinney National Airport
items.summary: WASHINGTON — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) today announced it issued McKinney National Airport a Part 139 Airport Operating Certificate, which allows the airport to accommodate commercial passenger airline service. This marks the first time a Texas airport has received an Airport Operating Certificate since 2005.

items.title: FAA Proposes $260,868 Fine Against ExcelAire, LLC for Alleged Illegal Operations
items.summary: WASHINGTON — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposes a $260,868 civil penalty against ExcelAire, LLC of New York and Georgia for allegedly conducting unauthorized charter operations. The FAA alleges that in August 2025, ExcelAire operated two flights for compensation or hire after the company’s director of operations surrendered the company’s air carrier certificate to the FAA in June 2025, when that person, and the remainder of the company’s required management personnel, resigned.

items.title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers State-of-the Art Air Traffic Control Management Tool to Transform The Flying Experience, Reduce Delays & Cancellations For the Traveling Public
items.summary: Cutting-edge platform – called SMART – centralizes 200 data streams to produce recommendations that will improve how the airspace is managed and flights are scheduled.

items.title: Laser Strikes on Aircraft Continue to Drop But Are Still Too High
items.summary: WASHINGTON -- For the third year in a row, reported laser strikes in the National Airspace System are down. Pilots reported 4,470 laser strikes to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in 2026 - a 24 percent decrease from this time last year. The FAA conducts outreach and training with local, state, and federal law enforcement to combat laser strikes. The outreach has resulted in a significant decrease in laser strikes which reached an all-time high of 13,304 in 2023.

items.title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces First Virginia College to Join Air Traffic Controller Training Program
items.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has partnered with Shenandoah University in Virginia to join the Enhanced Air Traffic – Collegiate Training Initiative (E-CTI) . Students who pass the E-CTI program can apply to become a controller on a fast track – skipping the FAA Academy in Oklahoma City and jumping straight to on-site facility training.
